\begin{abstract}
Flood-response streams may contain repeated, incomplete, and conflicting
reports that must be consolidated before teams are assigned. We study a
product similarity that gates temporal and contextual compatibility by
geographic proximity, followed by graph clustering and a bounded,
duplicate-aware priority heuristic. The mathematical result is conditional:
in its finite threshold region, every retained product edge has an explicit
distance bound, while a component bound additionally depends on its observed
hop diameter. Evaluation uses a frozen synthetic generator with
\RevisionClaim{gate1.protocol.seed_counts.development} development,
\RevisionClaim{gate1.protocol.seed_counts.calibration} calibration, and
\RevisionClaim{gate1.protocol.seed_counts.test} untouched test datasets.
On the label-aware track, product Louvain has mean ARI
\RevisionClaim{clustering.summary.benchmark_label_aware.product_louvain.ari_labeled_reports.mean};
the paired additive-minus-product difference is
\RevisionClaim{clustering.paired.benchmark_label_aware.additive_louvain.vs.product_louvain.ari_labeled_reports.mean}
with 95\% CI
[\RevisionClaim{clustering.paired.benchmark_label_aware.additive_louvain.vs.product_louvain.ari_labeled_reports.paired_confidence_interval.0},
\RevisionClaim{clustering.paired.benchmark_label_aware.additive_louvain.vs.product_louvain.ari_labeled_reports.paired_confidence_interval.1}].
This is not universal dominance: product rejects no noise and averages
\RevisionClaim{clustering.summary.benchmark_label_aware.product_louvain.false_operational_destinations.mean}
false destinations, whereas ST-DBSCAN trades lower ARI for much stronger noise
rejection. Exact duplicates leave the revised priority unchanged, but a
coordinated high-confidence campaign makes its drift worse than the legacy
score. Independent dispatch outcomes show no benefit over the legacy policy
and favor nearest-first on harm and deadlines in the tested scenarios.
Consequently, this is a synthetic methodological study, not field validation
or a deployment claim.
\keywords{Flood rescue \and Product similarity \and Graph clustering \and
Synthetic evaluation \and Priority heuristic.}
\end{abstract}

\section{Introduction}

Disaster-response streams combine spatial observations, evolving conditions,
and repeated descriptions of the same physical incident. Treating each report
as a destination can waste travel capacity; clustering solely by coordinates
can merge distinct incidents that overlap geographically or split one incident
reported across several sites. A coordinator also needs to inspect uncertainty
and policy trade-offs before using any cluster ranking.

We investigate a pipeline that converts each report into observable
attributes, constructs a spatial--temporal--contextual graph, detects
communities, and computes a bounded cluster-priority heuristic. Its central
composition is a product similarity: geography multiplies, and can veto, the
temporal--contextual term. Multiplicative similarities are established
technology---bilateral filtering uses the same structural
idea~\cite{tomasi1998bilateral}---so the product form is not claimed as novel.
Nor do we claim a Mercer or positive-semidefinite kernel on the Haversine
domain. The narrower question is whether a fully specified product-similarity
pipeline has a useful edge-localization property and how it behaves under
calibrated, held-out synthetic comparison.

The contributions are:
\begin{itemize}
\item a complete threshold-domain statement for product and additive
similarities, including a strict product edge bound and a component corollary
conditional on observed hop diameter;
\item a leakage-controlled protocol with disjoint development, calibration,
and test seeds, two calibration tracks, tuned direct baselines, operational
burden metrics, factorial diagnostics, and one sealed held-out run; and
\item a duplicate-aware priority stress test and algebraically independent
dispatch simulation that retain adverse results. These experiments establish
exact-duplicate invariance but do not validate a rescue policy.
\end{itemize}

\section{Related Work}

\paragraph{Crisis sensing and deployment context.}
CrisisMMD~\cite{alam2018crisismmd} and FloodNet
~\cite{rahnemoonfar2021floodnet} support multimodal disaster analysis.
Lightweight models such as MobileNetV3~\cite{howard2019mobilenetv3},
DistilBERT~\cite{sanh2019distilbert}, and
EmergencyNet~\cite{kyrkou2020emergencynet} motivate on-device attribute
extraction. Our generator supplies flood and urgency observations; we do not
evaluate a vision/language model, device latency, energy, or field network.
Edge extraction is therefore deployment context rather than an empirical
contribution.

\paragraph{Graph and spatio-temporal clustering.}
Louvain~\cite{blondel2008louvain} and
Leiden~\cite{traag2019leiden} optimize weighted modularity without a preset
cluster count. DBSCAN~\cite{ester1996dbscan}, HDBSCAN
~\cite{campello2013hdbscan}, and ST-DBSCAN~\cite{birant2007stdbscan} represent
density-based alternatives; the latter explicitly joins spatial, temporal,
and non-spatial criteria. Spatial constraints also appear in ClustGeo
~\cite{chavent2018clustgeo}, contiguity-constrained regionalization
~\cite{assuncao2006efficient}, and broader spatially constrained clustering
~\cite{yuan2021spatial}. These methods make clear that geographic compactness,
spatio-temporal density, and graph partitioning are not new in isolation.

\paragraph{Priority and humanitarian allocation.}
Multi-criteria allocation treats objectives and weights as policy choices
~\cite{saaty1980ahp,vitoriano2011multicriteria}. Humanitarian logistics exposes
real tension among equity, efficiency, and efficacy
~\cite{gralla2014review,huang2012models}. A bounded score is therefore not a
validated policy: evaluation must use outcomes that do not algebraically
repeat the score, and it must retain trade-offs against simpler dispatch
rules.

\section{Method}

\subsection{Observable Report Representation}

A report is represented as
\[
v_i=(L_i,T_i,F_i,E_i,N_i,V_i,C_i),
\]
where $L_i,T_i$ are location and time; $F_i,E_i\in[0,1]$ are reported flood
and urgency evidence; $N_i,V_i$ are reported demand and vulnerability
evidence; and $C_i\in[0,1]$ is an interpretable provenance/corroboration
heuristic. $N_i$ and $V_i$ are not treated as counts of unique people because
the reports have no validated person-identity linkage. Latent incident
identifiers, unique population, vulnerability truth, deadlines, and harm
parameters are available only to the synthetic evaluator and are prohibited
from clustering, tuning, and priority inference.

Confidence is computed only from observable provenance signals such as image
availability and corroborating payloads. It gates $E,F,N,$ and $V$
consistently, but is neither a truth probability nor a misinformation
detector. The recorded compact application JSON occupies
\RevisionClaim{runtime.packet.min_bytes}--\RevisionClaim{runtime.packet.max_bytes}
bytes (median \RevisionClaim{runtime.packet.median_bytes}) over
\RevisionClaim{runtime.packet.n_packets} reports. These values exclude
transport framing, HTTP/MQTT headers, TLS, authentication, retransmission, and
link-layer overhead.

\subsection{Product Similarity and Localization Domain}

Let $d_{ij}$ be Haversine distance and $\Delta t_{ij}$ absolute time
difference. Define
\begin{align}
G(d)&=\exp[-d^2/(2\sigma^2)],&
T(\Delta t)&=\exp[-\Delta t/\tau_t],\\
C(i,j)&=\exp[-|F_i-F_j|/\tau_F-|E_i-E_j|/\tau_E],\\
w^\times_{ij}&=G(d_{ij})[\beta T(\Delta t_{ij})+\gamma C(i,j)],
\label{eq:product}
\end{align}
where $\alpha,\beta,\gamma\ge0$, $\sigma>0$, and
$B=\beta+\gamma$. An edge is retained exactly when $w_{ij}>\theta$; a later
$k$-nearest sparsifier may delete but never add edges.

\begin{theorem}[Product edge localization]\label{thm:product}
If $B>0$ and $0<\theta<B$, every retained product edge satisfies
\[
d_{ij}<r^\times_\theta
 :=\sigma\sqrt{2\log(B/\theta)}.
\]
If $\theta\ge B$, the strict retained set is empty; for $\theta\le0$ there is
generally no non-trivial threshold-induced finite cutoff.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Because $T,C\in[0,1]$,
$w^\times_{ij}\le B\exp[-d_{ij}^2/(2\sigma^2)]$. In the finite region,
\[
\theta<w^\times_{ij}
\le B\exp[-d_{ij}^2/(2\sigma^2)]
\]
and strict monotonicity of the logarithm gives the stated radius. If
$\theta\ge B$, the maximum possible weight cannot exceed the threshold. For
$\theta\le0$, choosing $T=C=1$ retains arbitrarily distant finite model
points. Degenerate $B=0$ cases follow from $w^\times=0$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Conditional component bound]\label{cor:component}
In the finite product region, a connected vertex set with at least two
vertices and unweighted hop-diameter $h<\infty$ has geographic diameter
$D<h\,r^\times_\theta$.
\end{corollary}

The corollary follows from the triangle inequality along a path of at most
$h$ retained edges. A singleton is handled separately with $h=D=0$. It is not
an ex-ante compact-cluster guarantee: the pipeline does not enforce a useful
$h$, and a long retained chain may approach the bound. Moreover, calibrated
graph thresholds are weight quantiles, so the numerical radius is known only
after the selected threshold is realized.

For the controlled additive composition
\[
w^+_{ij}=\alpha G(d_{ij})+\beta T(\Delta t_{ij})+\gamma C(i,j),
\]
the correct contrast is threshold-dependent. If $\alpha>0$ and
$B<\theta<B+\alpha$, every retained edge satisfies
\[
d_{ij}<r^+_\theta
 :=\sigma\sqrt{2\log\!\left(\frac{\alpha}{\theta-B}\right)}.
\]
At $\theta\ge B+\alpha$ the retained set is empty, while at
$\theta\le B$ there is generally no non-trivial threshold-induced geographic
cutoff because the non-geographic contribution can retain arbitrarily distant
pairs. Thus addition does have a finite region; claiming otherwise would
overstate Theorem~\ref{thm:product}.

\subsection{Duplicate-Aware Bounded Priority Heuristic}

Exact-payload reports are collapsed by a fingerprint over observable
location, time, measurements, provenance, and missingness fields. Observable
near duplicates are coalesced by fixed geographic, temporal, measurement,
confidence, and missingness tolerances. Let $g$ index the resulting evidence
families. After clipping $C,F,E$ to $[0,1]$, $N$ to $[0,N_{\rm cap}]$, and
$V$ to $[0,V_{\rm cap}]$, the revised estimator is
\begin{align}
\widehat E&=
\frac{\sum_g\max_{i\in g}(C_iE_i)}
     {\max\{1,\sum_g\max_{i\in g}C_i\}},&
\widehat F&=\max_g\max_{i\in g}(C_iF_i),\\
\widehat N&=\max_g\max_{i\in g}(C_iN_i),&
\widehat V&=\max_g\max_{i\in g}(C_iV_i),\\
\widetilde N&=\min\!\left\{1,
\frac{\log(1+\widehat N)}{\log(1+N_{\rm ref})}\right\},&
A&=1+(\mu-1)\tanh(\widehat V/s),\\
R&=\omega_E\widehat E+\omega_F\widehat F+\omega_N\widetilde N,&
\mathcal P&=A R.
\label{eq:priority}
\end{align}
The maxima for $N,V$ deliberately avoid asserting that overlapping reported
counts are disjoint. With non-negative normalized weights and
$1\le\mu\le2$, $\mathcal P\in[0,2]$. The locked policy uses
$N_{\rm ref}=500$ and $V_{\rm cap}=50$; neither these caps nor the weights have
expert validation. The legacy ablation preserves report multiplicity and raw
summation, including a confidence bypass for $V$.

\section{Experimental Design}

\subsection{Frozen Synthetic Data}

The method-agnostic Gate-1 freeze contains
\RevisionClaim{gate1.data_contract.n_datasets} independently generated
datasets, \RevisionClaim{gate1.data_contract.n_reports} reports, and
\RevisionClaim{data.distribution.overall.scope.n_incidents} latent physical
incidents. The disjoint split is
\RevisionClaim{gate1.protocol.seed_counts.development} development,
\RevisionClaim{gate1.protocol.seed_counts.calibration} calibration, and
\RevisionClaim{gate1.protocol.seed_counts.test} test seeds. The held-out split
contains \RevisionClaim{data.quality.split_summaries.test.n_reports_total}
reports, ranging from
\RevisionClaim{data.quality.split_summaries.test.n_reports_min} to
\RevisionClaim{data.quality.split_summaries.test.n_reports_max} per dataset.

The generator varies incident geometry, report counts and dispersion,
time/context overlap, missing fields, provenance, exact and near duplicates,
unlinked noise, and coordinated campaigns. Each incident has latent
$N_{\rm true}$, $V_{\rm true}$, service demand, deadline, and a piecewise
lateness-harm curve. This richer internal truth supports error analysis, but
the family is still designed by the authors. It cannot establish external
validity for real floods.

\subsection{Calibration, Baselines, and Leakage Control}

Two pre-specified tracks use the same search ceilings and operational
constraints. The benchmark track may use calibration labels to maximize ARI.
The operational track is label-free and uses reverse-order partition
stability, retained density, connectivity, diameter, and review-burden
constraints. Graph thresholds are calibration-derived weight quantiles rather
than shared raw thresholds across incompatible scales. Product composition
comparisons additionally require matched retained fraction and mean degree.

The registry contains product and additive Louvain, a fixed seven-point convex
similarity mixture (not learned multiple-kernel clustering), ST-DBSCAN,
standardized DBSCAN/HDBSCAN, spatially constrained agglomerative, and
same-representation Leiden/spectral diagnostics. Calibration promoted
\RevisionClaim{gate2.selection.selection_count} feasible method--track
configurations and authentically retained
\RevisionClaim{gate2.selection.no_feasible_count} method--track exclusions.
The exclusions are not converted into poor test scores or silently removed.

The test split remained sealed until the protocol and selections were hashed.
The candidate suite then ran once without seed, method, track, resume, or
output filters. It produced
\RevisionClaim{gate3.coverage.selected_method_seed_rows} selected
method--seed rows and
\RevisionClaim{gate3.coverage.exclusion_seed_rows} retained exclusion rows
over \RevisionClaim{gate3.coverage.test_seed_count} test seeds, with no
prediction or scientific-seed failure.

\subsection{Endpoints and Inference}

Clustering co-primary families are (i) ARI on labeled reports, (ii) incident
split and merge loss, and (iii) false operational destinations and operator
review burden over all reports. Noise rejection/absorption and destination
geographic diameter are key secondary endpoints. Noise label $-1$ is never a
destination. The standard review policy counts each unresolved report as one
queue item.

Factorial diagnostics evaluate all on/off combinations of geography, time,
context, and $k$-nearest pruning, plus confidence, vulnerability, and
aggregation factors for priority. Main effects are paired factorial contrasts,
not causal estimates, and must be read with interactions and unmatched cells.

Priority stress tests include exact/near duplicates, low-confidence inflation,
coordinated high-confidence campaigns, and missing provenance. Dispatch uses
three resource scenarios and latent outcomes that do not algebraically reuse
priority, flood, vulnerability, or reported demand. We report latent harm,
deadline misses, arrival mean/max/CVaR, equity gap, workload, and
deadline-reached unique population; no single endpoint defines a winning
policy.

Across test seeds, summaries report mean, standard deviation, median, paired
bootstrap 95\% CI, paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test, effect size, and
denominator. Holm adjustment is applied within declared endpoint families.
All ties, adverse comparisons, failures, and unavailable pairs are retained.

The analytic edge property therefore did not imply empirical compactness
superiority.

\subsection{Runtime and Representation Scope}

The development-only Exp22 audit used
\RevisionClaim{runtime.contract.warmup_repeats} warm-up and
\RevisionClaim{runtime.contract.measured_repeats} measured isolated workers
with the thread limit set to
\RevisionClaim{runtime.contract.thread_limit}. At
\RevisionClaim{runtime.size.1494.n_events} events, median dense and
geographic-candidate-pruned total times are
\RevisionClaim{runtime.size.1494.dense_total_s.median}\,s and
\RevisionClaim{runtime.size.1494.spatial_total_s.median}\,s. Edge counts,
matrices (tolerance $10^{-9}$), and partitions agree for all three measured
sizes.

The spatial path prunes candidate-pair computation but still materializes a
dense $O(n^2)$ compatibility matrix. The result supports exact geographic
candidate pruning on the recorded one-core environment; it does not support
fully sparse memory scaling, field real-time performance, or an end-to-end
network-packet claim.

\section{Discussion and Threats to Validity}

\paragraph{Supported claims.}
The complete threshold analysis establishes a strict edge-localization
property for product similarity and a conditional hop-diameter corollary.
Under two frozen calibration tracks and one untouched synthetic run, product
Louvain has higher ARI than the calibrated additive composition. Exact-payload
deduplication makes the revised priority invariant to exact multiplicity.
These statements have analytic or locked held-out support.

\paragraph{Necessary qualifications.}
Product is not uniformly superior. Leiden ties Louvain; additive has a smaller
destination diameter; ST-DBSCAN markedly improves split/noise behavior while
worsening merge loss and ARI; product emits many false destinations. Factorial
main effects interact and include
\RevisionClaim{gate3.retention.factorial_density_match_failures}
density-unmatched cells. The high-confidence campaign defeats the intended
priority safeguard. Revised priority has no demonstrated latent-harm advantage
over legacy and is inferior to nearest-first for harm/deadlines in the shown
scenarios. These negative results prohibit claims of misinformation
robustness, dispatch benefit, or operational policy validation.

\paragraph{Synthetic and policy validity.}
All reports, incidents, duplicates, and latent outcomes are generated. Multiple
seeds measure variation within this generator family, not transfer to real
floods. No authorized incident-level real dataset or rescue/logistics expert
panel is available. Consequently, weights, caps, near-duplicate tolerances,
review rules, and dispatch resources are illustrative. The arithmetic
latitude/longitude centroid is metadata rather than a geodesic optimum.
External collection, annotation, privacy, and expert protocols are specified,
but executing them remains future work.

\paragraph{Method and inference validity.}
ARI uses labeled reports, while split/merge, noise, destinations, and review
burden expose different failures. Holm adjustment controls declared families
but does not eliminate generator dependence. The convex comparator is a fixed
mixture grid, not learned multiple-kernel clustering. Several registered
methods had no feasible configuration and remain explicit exclusions.
Community detection depends on resolution and graph sparsification; the
component theorem does not control $h$. The locked result preserves
scenario-family tables, including a multimodal-focused family, but G0 does not
expose a multimodal-specific claim selector. We therefore make no quantitative
multimodal claim; dedicated multimodal error analysis remains unresolved.

The single accepted held-out run identifier is:

\texttt{9797f31f-x0-exp23-heldout}.
\end{center}
Its manifest SHA-256 begins \texttt{cbedfe1c}, and its canonical result
content hash begins \texttt{ddafd634}. Gate 3 records one candidate invocation.
The G0 promotion includes a selector-compatible compact JSON, the complete
canonical result as a lossless gzip archive, the original
\RevisionClaim{promotion.audit.base_selector_count} selectors, audited
data/runtime tables, a numeric claim catalog, and generated LaTeX values.
Every empirical number above resolves through
\texttt{\textbackslash RevisionClaim} to that catalog. The one-command
\texttt{reproduce.sh} workflow verifies the companion artifact package,
recomputes selectors and publication values from the sealed result without
re-executing the held-out experiment, runs the tests, and rebuilds this PDF.
The package does not claim a public DOI or a clean immutable release commit
until those external submission steps are completed.

\section{Conclusion}

We presented a product-similarity graph and a bounded, duplicate-aware priority
heuristic for consolidating synthetic flood-rescue reports. The product form
has a finite-region edge bound, but cluster compactness remains conditional on
observed hop diameter. Calibrated held-out results favor product Louvain over
the additive composition on ARI in both tracks, while direct baselines reveal
important fragmentation, noise, diameter, and workload trade-offs. Exact
duplicates are neutralized, yet coordinated high-confidence reports remain a
failure, and independent dispatch outcomes do not validate the revised
priority policy. Real incident annotation, expert policy validation, and
fully sparse implementation are required before any deployment claim.
